note: One ASSISTANT entry announcing one call per tool, the TOOL_RESULTS entry answering them, and the user's reply to the ask_user question, projected through apptranscript. Each core tool ran for real against a temp workspace, recorded as cwd; notes marks the few outputs hand-written because their tool can't run in a test.

notes.call_apply_patch: A v4a patch updating one file and adding another.
notes.call_ask_user: A question put to the user, run for real: the tool posts it and answers with its fixed acknowledgement. toolWireAnswers, the user's reply, follows in the next turn.
notes.call_find_sessions: A search of the project's sessions for a phrase the earlier one said.
notes.call_find_sessions_catalog: The project's recent sessions, with no query: the earlier session and the recording one (its id, update time and project fixed).
notes.call_glob: A glob match: one path per match (sorted here).
notes.call_grep: A search in a path, filtered by a glob: one path:line:text line per hit (sorted, in the native fallback's form).
notes.call_job_list: The session's jobs, that one running (rows in a stable order).
notes.call_job_status: The job the timed-out command left running, checked: its id read from that call's result, then fixed.
notes.call_list_dir: A directory listing: one name and size per entry, then a blank line and the entry count.
notes.call_list_dir_empty: An empty directory: the count alone.
notes.call_list_dir_page: A page of a longer listing, paged with the tool's own limit (its default page is 1000 entries): the footer says how many of how many, and where the next page starts.
notes.call_mcp: Hand-written (needs an MCP server): an MCP tool, named <server>__<tool> the way agent/internal/mcp's manager namespaces it.
notes.call_mcp_hyphenated: Hand-written (needs an MCP server): an MCP tool whose server name had a hyphen (linear-app), which the manager turns into an underscore.
notes.call_read_file: A whole-file read: the output numbers each line.
notes.call_read_file_range: A read with an offset and a limit.
notes.call_read_transcript: An earlier session's transcript read as markdown (the default): its JSON envelope.
notes.call_read_transcript_outline: The same transcript read as an outline, whose envelope is flat.
notes.call_shell: A command run from the session's own directory, prefixed with cd to it: the output ends with its exit code.
notes.call_shell_failed: A command that exited 1: still a result, not an error, with [exit 1] at its end.
notes.call_shell_timeout: A command still running when its foreground wait timed out (this call's wait is 2s): it keeps running as a job, and the footer says so in several parts (its job id and the wait's seconds fixed, its state left off). It sleeps far longer than the recording takes, so the job calls after it always find it running until call_job_stop stops it.
notes.call_shell_windowed: A long output, windowed: a digest of its head and tail, then [exit 0 · output windowed — read more with read_transcript(...)] (its job id fixed, its state left off).
notes.call_task_list_add: Three tasks added to an empty list. Its state is the whole list, each task's store-minted times fixed.
notes.call_task_list_done: The first task done with a note; the daemon starts the next one itself, so the state shows task 2 in progress though the call never named it.
notes.call_task_list_view: A bare call: the list, changing nothing.
notes.call_unknown: Hand-written: a tool no step summary covers (no such tool exists); only its name matters.
notes.call_use_skill: A skill activation, the skill installed in the workspace. Its tool state (the session's random id, a digest of the rendered skill) changes every run, so it is left off.
notes.call_watch_inspect: The one-shot timer, inspected (created at the fixture's start).
notes.call_watch_list: The session's watches, both timers (each created at the fixture's start).
notes.call_watch_repeat: A repeating timer, with a note.
notes.call_watch_timer: A one-shot timer the session set for itself, with a note.
notes.call_web_fetch: Hand-written (web_fetch needs the network and a model): a fetched page's JSON result, with size_bytes.
notes.call_web_search: Hand-written (web_search needs the network and a model): one result per line.
notes.call_worktree_adopt: A worktree git made under the managed root without evener, adopted as a managed one.
notes.call_worktree_create: A worktree created from the repository's main branch; the session moves into it.
notes.call_worktree_exit: The session leaves the worktree for the main checkout.
notes.call_worktree_exit_again: The session leaves the worktree again, so it can be removed. The call and its result match the first exit's, so the registry appends its repetition nudge after the JSON.
notes.call_worktree_list: The repository's managed worktrees, and the lane git made without evener under unmanaged.
notes.call_worktree_prune: A prune with nothing it may remove: the removed worktree is still in its grace period, and the lane has no evener record.
notes.call_worktree_switch: The session moves back into the worktree.
notes.call_worktree_switch_again: A switch to the worktree the session is already in, which changes nothing.
